newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev eases on mark, rises vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev eases on mark, rises vs dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev eased to 998-1,000 per mark at the open from 997-1,000 at Wednesday's close on banks' and end-clients' higher foreign currency demand.
* End-lcients' mark purchases has pressured the lev in the past several days.
* Banks also built up foreign currency positions to profit on higher interest rates on mark and dollar deposits at home and a volatile mark/dollar on global markets.
* Interbank overnight lev deposit rates stand at 1.50-1.75 percent annually against 3.0 percent on overnight mark deposits and around five percent on dollar deposits.
* The lev rose to 1,830-1,835 to the dollar from 1,839-1,842 at Wednesday's close, tracking a mark/dollar rise on international markets.

* The lev has been pegged at 1,000 to the mark, which is an anchor currency under an IMF-prescribed currency board system. A currency board system is a fixed-exchange rate mechanism. It was introduced on July 1 to restore confidence in the lev.
* Under the system, Bulgaria's central bank pledged to buy and sell unlimited volumes of the anchor currency at a fixed bid of 995 levs and ask of 1,000 marks. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
